title: Spirit Airlines Prepares to Shut Down
partialText: The low-fare airline, which has struggled for years, had been trying to secure a $500 million lifeline from the Trump administration.

title: Schwab Affiliate Halts Customer Donations to Southern Poverty Law Center
partialText: Fidelity and Vanguard’s donor-advised fund entities have taken similar actions in the wake of a Justice Department indictment of the civil rights group.

title: Trump Administration Pushes Forward With Tariffs Based on Forced Labor Laws
partialText: Nonprofit groups have applauded an investigation on trade in goods made with forced labor but say that the Trump administration should go further to enforce its own laws

title: Oil Cools Slightly After a 4-Year High
partialText: The price of Brent crude, the international benchmark, dipped more than 2 percent a day after it rose above $120 a barrel in volatile trading.

title: F.D.A. Grants Early Access to Promising Drug for Pancreatic Cancer
partialText: Patients with one of the deadliest cancers have been pleading for an unapproved treatment that may prolong their lives.

title: Maryland Is First to Ban A.I.-Driven Price Increases in Grocery Stores
partialText: A state law that goes into effect in October prohibits grocery stores and third-party delivery services from using consumer data to boost prices.

title: Stocks and Oil Prices Sent Conflicting Signals in April Amid Havoc of Iran War
partialText: Energy markets remained disrupted by turmoil in the Middle East, while the S&P 500 posted its best month since November 2020.

title: Trump’s Tariff Reversal Reopens a Major Market for Scotch Whisky
partialText: A 10 percent tax on American imports was hurting British sales, even though exporters had increased sales in India, China and other countries.

title: Utility Bills Are Likely to Be Higher This Summer. Here’s What You Can Do.
partialText: The average bill is forecast to rise 8.5 percent. There are simple ways to make sure you’re not overpaying, like getting your air-conditioning checked.

title: OpenAI’s New Model Spurs Debate Over Computing Power
partialText: Sam Altman suggested it would be released more widely than a rival offering from Anthropic. Some are suggesting it’s because OpenAI has more computing power.

title: Fed Officials Cite Inflation Concerns in Defending Dissents
partialText: The Federal Reserve’s meeting this week was the most divisive in decades, a sign that President Trump’s pick to lead the central bank will face opposition if he pursues substantially lower interest rates.

title: Why U.S. Oil Companies Are Not Plugging the World’s Energy Gap
partialText: American producers are under pressure from investors to keep spending in check, and they are wary of drilling more wells because they are not sure oil prices will stay high.

title: Reporters at McClatchy Withhold Bylines in A.I. Dispute
partialText: Journalists at newspapers like The Miami Herald and The Sacramento Bee are refusing to let the chain use their names on summarized articles generated by a new A.I. tool.

title: The World’s Central Banks Are Wrestling With a Gigantic Problem
partialText: Inflationary surges and economic slowdowns set off by the war in Iran, tariffs and other Trump policies have forced monetary officials to adjust, our columnist says.

title: As Kentucky Derby Becomes a Bigger Business, Locals Feel Left Behind
partialText: Locals say rising ticket prices and a late start time for the Oaks race on Friday are hurting residents and restaurants. “The only thing I see is greed,” one steakhouse owner said.

title: Obamacare Enrollment Drops Sharply as Costs Rise
partialText: Americans can’t afford the higher health insurance premiums that resulted from Congress’s refusal to extend federal tax credits.

title: Why So Many People Already Own Shares of Elon Musk’s SpaceX
partialText: Even before the rocket company holds a major initial public offering, many people own stock in it through so-called special purpose vehicles.

title: Electric Cars Were a Big Deal Over a Hundred Years Ago
partialText: The very first E.V. was born in the 1830s. By the 1900s, electric carriages were dodging horse droppings in Manhattan streets.

title: 5 New Stockholm Bakeries
partialText: The Swedish appetite for sweets, caffeine and hanging out has led to a profusion of new convivial bakeries.

title: After Prison, a Financial Titan Plots an Unlikely Comeback
partialText: Bill McGlashan served time for trying to buy his son’s way into college during the Varsity Blues scandal. He hopes his new venture will restore his name — and save the planet.

title: Oil Companies’ Huge Profits Revive Calls for Temporary Windfall Taxes
partialText: European nations imposed temporary taxes in the 2022 energy shock when Russia invaded Ukraine, but whether they can effectively help households is up for debate.

title: Why Countries Are Stocking Up on Gold
partialText: As risk has escalated, central banks have bought more gold to stash in reserve. A widening Middle East war could add to the urgency.

title: Where in the World Is All That Gold Stored?
partialText: As central banks buy more gold, where to put all that heavy metal is an increasingly important question. Reserves must be secure and ready to trade in a crisis.

title: Crop Undercount Raises Questions About Reliability of U.S.D.A. Data
partialText: Corn estimates were off by 4.5 million acres last year. A lack of survey responses, not job cuts, led to the miss, the Agriculture Department said.

title: Behind Powell’s High-Stakes Decision to Stay at the Fed
partialText: Jerome H. Powell will remain a governor at the Federal Reserve after his term as chair ends, in a bid to guard against a further incursion by the Trump administration on the central bank’s independence.

title: U.S. Economy Grew 2 Percent in Early 2026 Even as War in Iran Began to Hit Energy Prices
partialText: Gross domestic product expanded at a 2 percent annual rate in the first three months of the year, a period including first weeks of conflict in the Middle East.

title: How Powell Just Complicated Trump’s Fed Plans
partialText: Traders now think the Federal Reserve will keep steady interest rates, or perhaps even increase them, amid succession intrigue at the central bank.

title: Casa, a Handyman Start-Up, Aims to Automate Home Maintenance
partialText: Casa, a company founded by former Uber executives, says it uses artificial intelligence and a stable of handymen to take care of members’ homes.

title: Senators Say Lawyers Helped Wealthy Clients Dodge Taxes in Puerto Rico
partialText: Rich Americans are writing off taxes they owed before they moved to Puerto Rico, the Senate Finance Committee says.

title: Palantir Is Making a French Chore Coat. Yes, That Palantir.
partialText: The data analysis company is selling a version of the jacket that it says will show its commitment to “re-industrializing America.”

title: With the Arrival of Goop Kitchen, Is New York Food Going Full L.A.?
partialText: Gwyneth Paltrow’s healthy-eating enterprise is just one of several recent Los Angeles exports to a rival city with its own ideas about what’s good.

title: Oil Price Hits Wartime High Above $120 a Barrel as Iran War Standoff Continues
partialText: Strong earnings and economic data buck fears that prolonged disruption to Middle East fuel supplies will eventually dent economic growth.

title: Rising Fuel Prices Force Policymakers to Weigh Excruciating Choices
partialText: The Bank of England and European Central Bank held interest rates steady on Thursday, as officials search for signs of possible longer-term damage and warn of the impact of a prolonged energy shock.

title: Roger Sweet, Creator of the He-Man Action Figure, Dies at 91
partialText: The musclebound character he developed as a toy designer for Mattel gave rise to the Masters of the Universe franchise and helped define the machismo of the 1980s.

title: Why the U.A.E. Is Quitting OPEC
partialText: The United Arab Emirates is walking away from OPEC this May. The New York Times’ energy reporter, Rebecca Elliott, breaks down how the war with Iran provided the perfect opening for the Emirates to go solo.

title: Ford Reports Higher Profit Thanks Partly to Tariff Refund
partialText: Ford Motor said it expected the federal government to refund $1.3 billion the company paid in tariffs that the Supreme Court later struck down.

title: Takeaways from Powell’s final news conference as Fed chair.

partialText: Beijing’s insistence that Meta unwind its deal with a Chinese A.I. start-up escalates the geopolitical fight over advanced tech.

title: Takeaways from Powell’s final Fed meeting as chair.
Powell Says He Will Stay On as Fed Governor After Term as Chair Ends
partialText: Jerome H. Powell cited lingering legal threats against him and the Federal Reserve in explaining his decision to remain at the central bank.

title: Bill Ackman’s I.P.O., Pershing Square USA, Raises $5 Billion
partialText: The initial public offering of Mr. Ackman’s new fund, Pershing Square USA, raised $5 billion.

title: World Bank estimates energy prices will surge 24 percent in 2026.
partialText: Iran war is fueling inflation and slowing growth around the world, according to a new report.

partialText: The central bank’s interest rate policy influences car and home loans, credit cards, savings accounts and more.

partialText: The chief executive, Scott Kirby, said that buying a smaller airline might not be worth the effort.

partialText: The Senate Banking Committee advanced Kevin Warsh’s nomination as Fed chair on Wednesday, teeing up the full chamber to hold a vote soon.

partialText: In partnership with Expedia, the ride-booking, food-delivering, package-transporting service takes another step toward becoming a super app.

partialText: Both entities cited the Justice Department investigation into the civil rights organization in messages to its charitable account holders.

partialText: The Federal Communications Commission is clashing again with the media giant. It’s another warning about the costs of angering President Trump.

partialText: Crude oil prices hit a fresh high since the start of the war in Iran, as energy supplies from the Middle East remain disrupted.
